messages:
ben_sre: Heads up: Scheduled failover of the us-west-2 edge pool + coordinated internal loadtest this Thu 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC -> 02:40 UTC (40m). Goal: exercise fallback routing + measure cold-KV behavior. Minimal customer impact expected, but we may see elevated p99 latency for ~5-10m during the cutover. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/edge-failover-2026-03-12

deploy-bot: Scheduled maintenance created: edge-pool-failover-usw2 at 2026-03-12T02:00Z (creator: ben_sre)

devinfra: Quick Q: what's the cutover sequence? Canary -> ramp? Are we draining active connections first?

ben_sre: Yes. Plan: 1) canary 10% traffic to region-b fallback for 5m, 2) validate p99 & 5xx, 3) ramp to 50% then 100%. Drain edge pods before full cutover. Example drain command: `kubectl -n inference drain pod/<pod> --ignore-daemonsets`.

jordan_oncall: I'll own oncall for the window. Pager coverage confirmed. Rollback = revert routing prefix + scale fallback back down.

simon_ml: We'll enable debug traces + retain KV cache metrics. Please tag traces with `failover-2026-03-12`.

maria_product: Do we need a customer-facing notice or should CS be pre-briefed?

ben_sre: No GA notice planned (low risk). CS on standby; I'll post to #customer-status if impact >15m.

devinfra: Loadtest details: we'll run internal stress tool after full cutover. Example: `stress-gen --target https://api.redwood.internal --qps 200 --duration 10m`. Aim is cold-cache p50/p90/p99 profiling.

ops-bot: Reminder: maintenance-policy exclusion applies; hosted API SLO (99.9% availability) unchanged. Short p99 spikes during the scheduled window are excluded per policy.

jordan_oncall: Creating incident ticket INC-2026-3247 to attach traces/graphs during window.

ben_sre: :thumbsup: Thanks team. Posting final schedule in #announcements now and creating a status page entry. Ping me @ben_sre for any blockers or if you want to run extra pre-checks.
